title: proof-bridge-forwarder-architectural-notes
content:
Purpose
This is a working architecture + ops note for the Proof Bridge Forwarder (PBF): the lightweight adapter that transforms internal control evidence and audit logs into target SIEM/archival formats while enforcing RBAC v2 access controls, retention/TTL rules, and chain-of-custody metadata.

Status and intent
- Draft: intended to consolidate design decisions before a proposal PR.
- Covers: message envelope, audit log schema mapping, export modes, RBAC V2 enforcement points, operational playbook for evidence incidents, sample retention/TTL rules, and canary rollout plan.
- Not final: still need security review for key management integration and threat modelling.

High-level goals
1) Deterministic exports: identical exports for identical evidence across hosts (idempotency).
2) Least-privilege access: RBAC v2 gates every action that reads/exports evidence artifacts.
3) Observable and auditable: every export produces a proof-record stored with the evidence (export provenance).
4) Resilient: support streaming and batch export with exactly-once semantics where possible; graceful degradation to S3 spillover.

Architecture overview
- Producers: control-plane components (RBAC service, enrollment service), runtime agents (collector sidecars, capture-runner), and audit-log aggregator.
- Proof Bridge Forwarder (PBF): stateless adapter running in dedicated security namespace. Responsibilities: validate envelope, enrich with RBAC assertion, canonicalize audit schema, apply redaction/PII filters per policy, route export to sink (SIEM, cloud-archive, external customer endpoint).
- Sink adapters: SIEM connector (CEF/Elastic Common Schema), Splunk HEC, Syslog/TLS, S3 manifest batches, and an HTTPS push target for channel partners.
- Store: short-term export ledger (Postgres) for proof-records, and long-term archive (S3 with server-side encryption + manifest).

Message envelope (canonical)
- envelope_id: UUID v4
- produced_at: ISO8601 timestamp
- producer_service: string (e.g., capture-runner-v2)
- evidence_id: stable id (string) — used to correlate artifacts
- evidence_type: enum [audit-event, control-artifact, snapshot, binary-blob]
- payload_format: mime/type (application/json, application/ndjson, application/octet-stream)
- payload_ref: either inline payload (if < 64KB) or signed S3 URL
- actor: {actor_id, actor_type}  <-- note: in PBF implementation this will be normalized into actor_id and actor_origin fields
- rbac_assertion_id: id of the RBAC v2 assertion used to authorize this export
- retention_hint: seconds (optional) — consumer hint for TTL
- chain_of_custody: list-of-handlers (string list) serialized as a single string in envelope
- signature: base64 sig of envelope by producer (for provenance)

Sample audit log schema (canonical fields we use inside PBF)
- event_id: string (uuid)
- ts: ISO8601
- actor_id: string
- actor_roles: comma-separated roles (RBAC v2 compressed)
- action: string (e.g., policy.evaluate, token.create)
- resource: string (resource path)
- outcome: string (success|failure|partial)
- evidence_id: string (links to evidence store)
- evidence_hash: sha256 hex
- source_host: fqdn or ip
- context: free-form JSON string (small)

RBAC V2 enforcement model in PBF
- Enforcement points:
  - Inbound validation: ensure rbac_assertion_id present and issued by RBAC service.
  - Enrichment: query RBAC service to map assertion -> expanded roles & allowed destinations.
  - Destination check: ensure the requested sink is permitted for that assertion (e.g., no external endpoints for PII-tagged evidence unless explicit allow).
- Tokens and rotation: PBF uses short-lived mTLS certs for sink-to-sink auth; RBAC assertions embed audience claims for sinks.
- Audit trail: PBF persists a proof-record (export ledger) for every attempted export with fields [envelope_id, event_id, sink, result, timestamp, ledger_signature].

Export modes and failure modes
1) Streaming (preferred): push as soon as event arrives, low-latency. Backpressure: use bounded in-memory buffer + circuit breaker. On transient sink failure -> retry with exponential backoff.
2) Batched: group by tenant, compress, and send on schedule (1–5 min windows). Good for high-throughput low-latency-sensitive telemetry.
3) Spillover archive: if runtime or sink unavailable > 15 minutes, write signed manifests to S3 with metadata and schedule an import job.
4) Edge-case: if envelope signature invalid -> reject with 403 and persist rejection reason.

Exactly-once and idempotency guidance
- Use envelope_id + sink as idempotency key.
- For streaming sinks that do not support dedupe (syslog), persist last-sent sequence in export ledger and compare.
- For batch/S3 flow, include manifest checksum and evidence_hash to detect duplicates.

Privacy/redaction rules (high level)
- All evidence labeled with PII_SENSITIVITY (low, medium, high) by capture-runner. PBF enforces: do not export high PII to external-sinks without DLP-approval flag.
- Redaction hooks: regex-based PII filters + field-level redaction based on schema.
- Tokenization option: PBF supports reversible tokenization for partner exports using key-wrapping (KMS) — requires approval and explicit retention policy.

Operational runbook (concise)
- S1: SIEM connector failure (HEC 503 spikes)
  - Alert: SIEM-Export-Errors > 5/min for 3m
  - Action: flip PBF -> batched mode for affected tenant(s), escalate to infra, open incident, engage SIEM ops.
  - Mitigation: increase retry window, enable spillover to S3, mark export-ledger entries with "delayed" tag.
- S2: Evidence mismatch detected (hash mismatch)
  - Alert: Export-Ledger-Hash-Mismatch
  - Action: mark evidence as quarantined, trigger replay job from source canonical store, record incident, notify product-owner.
- S3 spillover recovery
  - Periodic import job picks up manifests. Import job verifies ledger_signature -> if valid, replay into sink with same envelope_id to preserve idempotency.

Canary/cutover plan (minimal safe path)
- Stage A: deploy PBF in staging with SIEM mirrors of production (no outward traffic).
- Stage B: enable export for 5% of tenants to new PBF (split by tenant id hash). Monitor metrics: latency, success-rate, duplicate-exports.
- Stage C: increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24–48h observation windows.

Monitoring and metrics (must emit)
- pbf.export.latency (p50/p95/p99)
- pbf.export.success_rate by sink
- pbf.buffer.overflow.count
- pbf.spillover.count
- pbf.redaction.invocations

Open questions / TODOs
- Concurrence with RBAC team: add audience claim to v2 assertions? (JIRA-SEC-824)
- KMS integration model for reversible tokenization - key-rotation SOP needed.
- DLP rules: need concrete regex set and test corpus from product security.
- Threat model review for envelope signing and ledger-proof persistence (needs crypto review).

Appendix: example envelope (ndjson for clarity)
{"envelope_id":"f1b2c3d4-9e7a-4b0b-8f2a-0a1b2c3d4e5f","produced_at":"2026-02-28T16:42:10Z","producer_service":"capture-runner-v2","evidence_id":"ev-2026-02-28-0001","evidence_type":"audit-event","payload_format":"application/json","payload_ref":"s3://redwood-evidence-prod/ev-2026-02-28-0001.json?sig=...","actor_id":"user:alice@company.com","rbac_assertion_id":"assert-9f2b","retention_hint":"2592000","chain_of_custody":"capture-runner-v2 -> proof-bridge-01","signature":"base64sig=="}

Notes to reviewers
- This doc expects the RBAC team to expose a light-weight assertion lookup API (assertion_id -> {roles,allowed_sinks,tenant_id}). If that API is delayed, fallback behavior will be to treat unknown assertions as deny-by-default and route to quarantined-bucket.
- Please add comments inline or reference JIRA-SEC-824 for design decisions that must be prioritized.

Quick checklist before PR:
- [ ] Finalize envelope signature scheme (ed25519 vs RSA) and update SDKs.
- [ ] Harden PII redaction rules + test vectors.
- [ ] Add end-to-end test that simulates SIEM HEC 5xx and verifies spillover + replay.
- [ ] Create runbook page in Confluence from this note and link in alerts.

-- end of working note --
